summary.headline: Grasim Q4 FY26: Birla Opus revenue up 52% YoY like-to-like, Pivot revenue more than doubled; paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27 on crude-linked input cost spike.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as a record year, with consolidated revenue of INR1,75,431 crores and standalone revenue of INR41,039 crores. Birla Opus grew 52% YoY like-to-like in Q4 and crossed 10% revenue market share in March 2026 on its own, while Birla Pivot's Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY and is close to its INR8,500 crore annual guidance. Raw material costs linked to crude derivatives rose sharply, with management citing up to 20-25% of COGS, prompting two further paint price hikes staggered into Q1 FY27. Cellulosic fibre and cement (UltraTech) contributed strong profit growth, and Grasim announced a INR10 final dividend.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue roughly doubled vs FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Caustic soda sales volume Q4 FY26

segments.name: Birla Opus (paints)
segments.commentary: Q4 like-to-like revenue +52% YoY; revenue market share up ~90 bps QoQ and 370 bps in FY26, now No.3 in organised decorative paints and crossed 10% share in March 2026. Installed capacity 1,332 MLPA (24% of industry); Kharagpur plant commercialised in Q3 FY26. Network at 11,500 towns, 50,000+ dealers, 1,200+ franchise stores; 218 products.

segments.name: Birla Pivot (B2B e-commerce)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue more than doubled YoY; close to INR8,500 crore annual revenue guidance. Delivers to 5,000+ pin codes across 400+ cities. Management targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27, possibly sooner.

segments.name: UltraTech (cement, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Crossed 200 MTPA grey capacity in April 2026, targeting 240+ MTPA by March 2028. UltraTech declared INR240 per share dividend, implying about INR4,000 crore cash inflow to Grasim before tax.

segments.name: Cellulosic fibre (VFY/Lyocell)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR4,614 crores (+14% YoY), EBITDA INR588 crores. Harihar Lyocell Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa under way within a total 110,000 tpa expansion. China operating rates at 92% in Q4 versus 87% a year ago.

segments.name: Chemicals (CFI)
segments.commentary: Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA moving to 1,530 KTPA. Specialty chemicals revenue +5% YoY, but higher ECH input prices hit profitability. Specialty chemicals 27% and chlorine derivatives 22% of revenue mix.

segments.name: Aditya Birla Capital (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Board approved a INR4,000 crore preferential equity raise; Grasim to invest INR2,880 crores to keep its 52.3% fully diluted stake.

segments.name: Insulators (within Others)
segments.commentary: Porcelain capacity held flat with productivity focus only; polymer long rods sold out after recent expansion; hollow composite expansion being evaluated. Sales and EBITDA no longer disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry paint growth to move from single-digit to double-digit in FY27, with Birla Opus targeting high double-digit growth.

Birla Opus priorities in order: become No.2 decorative paints player, reach INR10,000 crore revenue in the third year of full-scale operations (FY26 treated as year one), then profitability. Paint EBITDA losses to narrow quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
Birla Opus dealer network to exceed 15,000 towns by end of FY27 from 11,500 currently.
Birla Pivot targets EBITDA break-even exit in FY27.
Two further paint price increases announced April 2026, staggered into Q1 FY27; consumer impact expected in second half of Q1 and all of Q2 FY27.
Capex guidance for FY27 to be shared next quarter.
Grasim intends to keep above 50% stake in UltraTech and Aditya Birla Capital (current position, not a long-term policy).
capex_capacity: UltraTech above 200 MTPA grey capacity (April 2026); 240+ MTPA target by March 2028.
Harihar Lyocell: Phase 1 of 55,000 tpa in progress, total 110,000 tpa expansion; Phase 2 to be announced.
Birla Opus Kharagpur (sixth plant) commercialised Q3 FY26; average distance travelled per product down over 30%.
Chlor-alkali capacity 1,505 KTPA to 1,530 KTPA; additional capacity under evaluation.
Insulators: no plans to add porcelain base capacity; incremental investment in polymer long rods and hollow composites.
demand_pricing: Paints: dealer price hikes of 2-6% in Jan-Feb 2026 were absorbed; primary and secondary sales stayed strong in Q4 and April 2026 primary sales were in line with March.
Paints: input costs rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS due to crude-linked raw materials, packaging and rupee depreciation; management says raw material prices remain unstable.
Paints: 10% free-paint consumer scheme continues despite price hikes; institutional channel grew 43% QoQ and 212% YoY, with a pipeline of 45,000 sites.
Paints premium and luxury products at 65% of value; 75% of products rated No.1 in blind tests by applicators (company claim).
Cellulosic fibre: management says cellulosic fibres are growing at roughly 2x the CAGR of other fibres in India; benign pulp prices supported margins.
Specialty chemicals: ECH input price increase compressed profitability.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth in paints will come from distribution expansion and tinting machines versus throughput?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth from both numerical dealer expansion (11,500 towns to 15,000+) and throughput gains by adding product ranges to existing dealers. Older dealers over 18 months show 25-50% higher counter share and throughput comparable to legacy players.

qa_highlights.question: Is paint profitability improving from scale, and is FY26 the first full year for the INR10,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed FY26 as the first full operating year internally. Fixed costs (sales and service force, brand spend) were front-loaded and should be covered by growth; variable-cost levers include better procurement, plant and logistics optimisation, and adding second and third raw material suppliers. Paint contribution improved significantly in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How close is Birla Opus to the No.2 position in decorative paints?
qa_highlights.answer: Birla Opus plus Birla White putty is roughly at the level of the current No.2 on a decorative-only basis for Q4 FY26. The ambition is for Birla Opus alone to become No.2 in decorative paints, excluding industrial.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer throughput versus industry benchmarks?
qa_highlights.answer: Throughput is in line with market presence across A/B/C/D dealer classes. Top dealers stock 2-2.5x the bottom dealer and generate 4-5x its throughput. The market leader is estimated to have 20-25% more dealers and a richer A-class mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital allocation plan after the UltraTech dividend, given about INR2,900 crores for ABC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the INR2,900 crore use (ABC stake maintenance) as a one-off for FY26. Cash is being used for Grasim's dividend, maintaining the ABC stake, and supporting the two new businesses. Capex guidance for FY27 will come next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pivot profitability path and when will segment disclosure start?
qa_highlights.answer: Pivot aims to exit FY27 at EBITDA break-even and may get there sooner. Paints EBITDA losses are on a glide path to narrow each quarter. Management said segment reporting for paints and Pivot would start shortly.

qa_highlights.question: Will paint EBITDA losses (about INR300 crores per quarter) come down materially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management answered 'Yes, it will come down' without quantifying the timing.

qa_highlights.question: Insulator capacity, sales and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Porcelain capacity is flat, with productivity focus; polymer long rods are sold out after expansion; hollow composite expansion is being evaluated. Insulator sales and EBITDA are no longer disclosed.

risks_watch: Paint input cost volatility: crude-linked raw materials and packaging rose to as high as 20-25% of COGS; management says prices remain unstable and could escalate further, so the staggered Q1 FY27 price hikes may not fully offset costs.

Demand elasticity: consumer and contractor impact of the price hikes expected in second half of Q1 and all of Q2 FY27; April 2026 primary sales were in line with March, and secondary sales are being tracked weekly.
Paints EBITDA losses (about INR300 crore per quarter per an analyst) are guided to narrow QoQ and YoY, but no quantified timeline was given; watch whether the glide path shows up in Q1 FY27.
Segment disclosure for Birla Opus paints and Birla Pivot is due to start shortly; the first disclosures will show the actual losses and Pivot's break-even progress.

FY27 capex guidance is pending and will be shared next quarter; capital allocation (dividend, ABC stake maintenance, support for new businesses) was described as a one-off for FY26, not a long-term policy.
key_quotes: The spiraling of cost of goods to as high as 20% to 25% of COGS and we are still counting the impact.

This VUCA situation makes demand forecasting difficult and we need to closely monitor the situation as impact of price rise will slowly be felt by consumers and contractors in second half of quarter one and entire quarter two FY '27.
Yes, this is a one-off measure. Yes, yes, absolutely.
No, no, we are not talking of a long-term policy. I am giving you the current allocation of fund.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident and assertive on paints share gains, Pivot growth and cellulosic fibre, but cautious on input costs, demand elasticity and the timing of paint losses. It was evasive on insulator sales and EBITDA, which it no longer discloses, and on the longer-term capital allocation policy, which it framed as a current position rather than a commitment.
